locations.name: Brackle Road
locations.blurb: Packed-dirt track that ties Funnis to the outside world. Wide enough for two wagons most of the way, it narrows in the hills and north of the village climbs into a foot-only trail toward the mountains.

locations.name: Funnis Bridge
locations.blurb: A plain-looking timber span over the ravine, built so well that loaded wagons cross at speed without a creak. It is the only road crossing, so all wheeled traffic passes under the sentries' eyes.

locations.name: Wagon Yard
locations.blurb: A broad stretch of firm, packed earth just across the bridge where carts turn, unload, or wait their turn to be looked over before the gate.

locations.name: Main Gate
locations.blurb: Two-story timber gatehouse set in the palisade, with archers on a covered walkway above heavy double doors. One leaf usually stays open by day, and unfamiliar faces are challenged.

locations.name: Sawmill
locations.blurb: A walled timber yard just outside the palisade, busy with stacked logs and planks around a tall windmill that powers the saws. A guild master directs the crews.

locations.name: Wayhouse
locations.blurb: The settlement's front desk, just inside the gate. Visitors give their names and business here, and petitions and trade requests are logged and passed to the right body.

locations.name: Gate Lodge
locations.blurb: Low, broad guest quarters near the gate with a big hearth and simple sleeping alcoves. Lodging is free but supervised, and the building is meant for welcome, not for lingering.

locations.name: First Voice Hall
locations.blurb: Hall for weighty matters: formal delegations, announcements, and judgment when consensus fails elsewhere. A great carved seat on a dais stands for the First Voice's borrowed authority.

locations.name: Market
locations.blurb: A communal exchange for extras rather than staples: fine woodwork, hides, charms, and curiosities. Trade is mostly barter, and activity rises and falls with the festival calendar.

locations.name: Council Lodge
locations.blurb: Where the six clan leaders meet in a circle of carved seats. No votes are taken; talk continues until agreement is reached, and the lodge often stands empty.

locations.name: Trade Hall
locations.blurb: The public face of Funnis commerce, where guild agents and known merchants settle contracts, delivery schedules, and dues for timber, wool, and crafted goods.

locations.name: Common Hall
locations.blurb: The informal heart of the village, with long tables and open hearths for shared meals, feasts, and naming and harvest celebrations. Invited guests are a rare honor here.

locations.name: Barns (north)
locations.blurb: Outlying barns and storehouses near the corrals, used for shearing, processing, and staging wool and goods awaiting trade.

locations.name: Barns (south)
locations.blurb: Barns near the southern wall, part of the scattered storehouses used for staging goods and surplus away from the central stores.

locations.name: Longhouses
locations.blurb: The clan dwellings that anchor village life. Each of the six clans keeps at least one, and larger clans keep more for extended families and visiting kin.

locations.name: Corrals
locations.blurb: Shared pens for the village sheep and goats, with weather shelters and separate gates for shearing and kidding. Chicken runs sit nearby, and herding duty rotates among the clans.

locations.name: North Gate
locations.blurb: A lightly guarded working gate used by herders, hunters, foragers, and fishers. Rarely barred by day, it opens onto trail posts pointing to fields and river bends.

locations.name: Watchtower (northeast)
locations.blurb: An outlying timber platform watching the northern approaches and nearby fields, an early warning post for travelers, beasts, or bandits.

locations.name: Watchtower (bridge)
locations.blurb: The tower at the settlement end of the bridge. Its sentries can see down Brackle Road and into the ravine, and signal the Main Gate before anyone arrives.

locations.name: Boat Launch
locations.blurb: Narrow stone-cut steps down the ravine to a calm reach of Clear Creek, where dugouts are kept for fishing and short trips. Outsiders rarely use the boats without an escort.

locations.name: Woods (north)
locations.blurb: Whispering Woods on the northern slopes, where pine begins to mix with the hardwoods as the land rises toward the Livingstone Mountains.

locations.name: Woods (southwest)
locations.blurb: Old forest beyond Whistling Run, where oak and beech shade fern and fungus. Game is plentiful, but the deeper woods grow stranger.

locations.name: Woods (southeast)
locations.blurb: Forest east of Clear Creek, crossed by quiet game trails. Bandits and smugglers sometimes try these paths to skirt the village, though few go unnoticed.
